response.title: can i use a solar generator in an apartment
response.answer:
Yes, you can use a solar generator in an apartment. In fact, portable solar generators are a good option for apartment dwellers who want backup electricity or to reduce their reliance on the grid.

However, there are some limitations, especially regarding where you can place the solar panels.

1. How a solar generator works in an apartment
Shop
Shop
Shop
Shop
Shop
Shop
Shop
Shop
Shop

A solar generator typically consists of two components:

Portable power station: A rechargeable battery that stores electricity and powers your devices.

Solar panels: Convert sunlight into electricity to recharge the battery.

You can also charge most portable power stations from a regular wall outlet, making them useful even without solar panels.

2. What you can power

A solar generator can power many apartment essentials, depending on its battery capacity and output rating.

Appliance

	

Typical power consumption




Wi-Fi router

	

10–20 W




Laptop

	

30–100 W




LED light

	

5–15 W




Television

	

50–150 W




Refrigerator

	

80–200 W while running




Window AC

	

500–1,500 W




Space heater

	

750–1,500 W

For example, a 1,000 Wh solar generator might power a 100 W television for approximately 8–9 hours, accounting for conversion losses.

Running air conditioning or electric heating requires much larger batteries.

3. Important apartment restrictions

Balcony: You may be able to place portable solar panels on your balcony, but check your lease and building rules before mounting anything.

Windows: Panels behind glass can generate electricity, but typically much less than outdoors.

Fire safety: Choose a reputable power station with appropriate safety certification, ideally UL 2743, and follow the manufacturer's charging and ventilation instructions. 
UL Solutions
+1

Electrical connections: Plug appliances directly into the power station. Never connect its output to an apartment wall outlet to power the building's wiring.

Gas generators: Never use a gasoline or propane generator indoors or on an apartment balcony.

4. What size should you get?

The best setup depends heavily on whether you're trying to save money on electricity or have backup power. Those two goals can require very different systems.
